title: Tenant-scoped fallback priority override causing cross-tier misroutes
creator: Maya Li
description: A recent change to the fallback comparator ranking allowed tenant-level override rules to take precedence over global tier affinity. In production this caused requests from two enterprise customers to be routed from Dedicated capacity into a hosted-compatible model variant in a different region and lower tier, violating expected SLAs and data residency constraints. Customers reported increased latency and one reported failed policy checks. This ticket tracks the hotfix, RCA, and long-term guardrails to prevent recurrence.

mitigation: Hotfix: reverted comparator change (PR #1109) in control-plane routing service and redeployed config to all regions

Customer communication: sent incident notification and offered dedicated investigation calls with SRE and Account teams
root_cause: A refactor intended to simplify fallback comparator evaluation changed the tie-breaking order: tenant-scoped rules were evaluated after global tier-affinity checks in the new code path. For certain tenants with explicit overrides, this caused the comparator to select a lower-cost hosted variant despite dedicated-pool affinity and region constraints. Insufficient unit/integration tests for tenant-scoped precedences and no canary traffic coverage for the change allowed the regression to reach production.
steps_taken: Reverted comparator ordering change in git commit abc123 (PR #1109) and deployed to control plane
Added an integration test that simulates tenant overrides vs tier affinity and verifies region constraints under high concurrency
Expanded smoke canary to include two enterprise tenants and dedicated pool health signals before full rollout
Added alert rule for tenant->model misroute rate with synthetic checks per-tenant
acceptance_criteria: No tenant experiences misroutes in staging under 10k synthetic requests representing peak traffic
Integration tests pass in CI with coverage for tenant overrides, region affinity, and fallback comparator tie-breaking
Canary rollout shows zero misroutes for the two previously impacted tenants over 72 hours
Post-deployment incident review completed and communicated to stakeholders
